title: Streaming a PC to a Switch and a 3DS

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A Nintendo 3DS from 2015 with a four hundred by two-forty top screen, streaming a PC game over Wi-Fi. Should that even work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'd have bet against it. Who does that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Antoine does, on the side. He maintains three homebrew repos that share one itch: run something interesting on hardware that wasn't designed for it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Artemis-Switch. It's his fork of Moonlight-Switch, wired for Apollo hosts, which is Sunshine-style streaming, instead of classic NVIDIA GameStream. He streams Steam Big Picture from his desktop and uses an in-app overlay.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A Quick tab with window-management shortcuts, keyboard presets and host scripts, handy when the host is a Windows box and the Switch is just the display. And a Performance tab: around twelve megabits per second in his capture, Wi-Fi bars, and receive, decode and render timings.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How do you read those timings?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Render is usually the bottleneck on the Switch. If receive and decode are under a millisecond, the network and decoder are healthy and the frame budget goes mostly to compositing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: moonlight-N3DS, a GameStream client for the New 3DS, which has extra RAM and CPU. Antoine's fork is where he experiments with build fixes. The constraints are brutal: software decode, an old handheld's Wi-Fi, so lower bitrate and higher latency than on the Switch. The win is simply having a Moonlight path at all. Most of the community interest, around three hundred stars, lives on the upstream repo.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: sm64coopdx-switch, a Switch port of the cooperative Super Mario 64 project, with online co-op and Lua mods. A legal note on the page: like every port, you supply your own legally obtained ROM. The repo builds the port, it doesn't ship game assets.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Curiosity, mostly. The full write-up has the overlay screenshot and links to all three repos.
